text:
Tommy Novak was a third-round pick in 2015 and spent years as an AHL scorer trying to stick. In Pittsburgh he's become one of the few forwards whose goals are winning games: eight goals in 20 games, five in his last ten, and his goals have added more wins than all but 36 skaters in the league.

There's a real player underneath the hot hand. The Penguins get 55% of the 5v5 expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, and Evolving-Hockey had him in the 96th percentile among forwards last season for how much his team created with him out there, 79th of 401 by wins above replacement. He's playing 16:19 a night lately, up more than a minute.

The finishing is the part to watch. He's shooting 22.9% against a talent range near 14%, and Pittsburgh has scored 5.2 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice. With the Penguins losing and the trade talk swirling around Erik Karlsson and Rickard Rakell, Novak's cheap production is one of the quieter positives. The shooting should come down; the chances say he's still a useful middle-six forward.
headline: Novak keeps finishing for Pittsburgh
